paragraphs: PPO is widely successful in reinforcement learning, but its theoretical foundations leave important questions open. This paper asks whether an optimistic version can learn effectively in linear Markov decision processes, a basic setting for studying reinforcement learning with function approximation. The authors develop a variant for episodic problems with adversarial rewards and full-information feedback.

The algorithm uses a new mechanism that organizes updates into multiple batches. Its analysis also introduces a covering-number argument for value and policy classes: a way of controlling the complexity of the collections of predictions and behaviors considered. Together, these ingredients support a regret guarantee of roughly d^(3/4) H² K^(3/4), suppressing logarithmic factors.

Here d describes the linear model dimension, H the episode length, and K the number of episodes. The sublinear dependence on K means average regret decreases as experience accumulates. The authors report the strongest regret bound among existing policy-based algorithms in the stated stochastic and full-information adversarial settings. This establishes a guarantee for their particular optimistic variant under these conditions.
neurips-2023-a-theoretical-analysis-of-o.tldr: An optimistic PPO variant achieves improved theoretical regret guarantees in linear decision processes using batched updates and a new complexity analysis.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether models benefit from representing the world similarly to humans. The focus is few-shot learning: making effective use of only a small number of examples. Rather than assuming that greater human similarity always improves performance, the authors develop an information-theoretic analysis that suggests a U-shaped relationship between representational alignment and few-shot performance.

A U-shaped relationship allows strong performance at both low and high alignment, with weaker performance between them. The authors examine 491 computer vision models and observe the predicted pattern empirically. This finding matters because it complicates a simple ranking in which every increase in human alignment should correspond to a better learner.

The study also finds that highly aligned models are more robust to natural adversarial attacks and domain shifts. Taken together, the results suggest that human-like representations are often sufficient for useful learning and generalization, but are not necessary. Models can succeed through other representational arrangements, and the observed relationship does not establish that increasing alignment will always improve an individual model.
neurips-2023-alignment-with-human-repres.tldr: Across 491 vision models, human representational alignment has a U-shaped relationship with few-shot performance, while highly aligned models show stronger robustness.

paragraphs: In k-medoids clustering, each cluster is represented by an actual data point. This makes its representative directly inspectable and allows clustering with arbitrary distance metrics, including those suited to unusual kinds of objects. BanditPAM already made this approach more computationally practical. This paper introduces BanditPAM++, which accelerates that algorithm while returning the same clustering solutions.

The improvement comes from recognizing two opportunities to reuse work. Some clustering information can be shared within a single iteration, and additional information can be carried across iterations. These structural observations reduce repeated computation. The resulting complexity improvement is an O(k) speedup relative to BanditPAM, where k is the number of clusters.

The authors also report substantial reductions in actual runtime, often by several times. On CIFAR10, BanditPAM++ produces the same results more than ten times faster. The contribution therefore improves the cost of obtaining an existing solution rather than trading solution quality for speed. A high-performance C++ implementation with Python and R interfaces makes the method accessible from common data-analysis workflows.
neurips-2023-banditpam-faster-k-medoids-.tldr: BanditPAM++ reuses clustering information within and across iterations to return BanditPAM’s solutions substantially faster.

paragraphs: Training a robust classifier requires accounting for harmful input perturbations, but estimating the worst possible loss is difficult. Adversarial training uses estimates that can fall below the true worst case, providing insufficient regularization for certification. Sound certified training uses upper bounds, but loose bounds can impose excessive regularization and reduce accuracy on ordinary inputs.

TAPS combines interval bound propagation, or IBP, with projected gradient descent, or PGD, training. The goal is to obtain more precise estimates of worst-case loss and reduce the excessive conservatism of certified training. Crucially, these training estimates are not necessarily sound: the method does not guarantee that its optimization objective always bounds the true worst-case loss.

Despite that qualification, the authors report improvements in both standard and certified accuracy, with state-of-the-art empirical results in many settings. One example reaches 22% certified accuracy on TinyImageNet for perturbations bounded by an infinity-norm radius of 1/255. The result shows that an unsound training approximation can still help produce networks with stronger measured certified performance.
neurips-2023-connecting-certified-and-ad.tldr: TAPS combines IBP and PGD training using tighter but potentially unsound loss estimates, empirically improving both ordinary and certified accuracy.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can generate high-quality images through processes described by stochastic differential equations. In practice, numerical solvers approximate these continuous processes with discrete steps, introducing error. This paper addresses that gap by fine-tuning pretrained diffusion models with a contrastive sampling chain, aiming to bring their generated distribution closer to the real data distribution.

The theoretical contribution connects the training objective to distributional accuracy. The authors show that an appropriate combination of contrastive loss and score matching upper-bounds the KL divergence between the data and model distributions. They use the contrastive loss to construct the fine-tuning chain, which reduces discretization error and the resulting distributional gap.

The method can be applied to different pretrained diffusion models, including models using fast sampling algorithms. Experiments demonstrate improvements in sample quality or modest sampling acceleration. For a pretrained EDM on CIFAR10, FID improves from 2.04 to 1.88 with 35 neural function evaluations. Alternatively, the method reaches the original 2.04 FID with 25 evaluations, illustrating a concrete quality-versus-computation trade-off.
neurips-2023-contrastive-sampling-chains.tldr: Contrastive fine-tuning reduces diffusion sampling discretization error, improving image quality or reaching comparable quality with fewer model evaluations.

paragraphs: A policy learned in one environment may perform poorly in another when the same action produces different consequences. This paper studies online adaptation with abundant source-domain data but limited interaction with the target domain. The motivating challenge is deciding which existing experience remains useful when the environment’s dynamics have changed.

Value-Guided Data Filtering, or VGDF, approaches this decision through value differences across domains. Instead of focusing only on how the dynamics differ, it selectively shares source transitions according to the closeness of paired value targets. These targets express the outcomes relevant to learning a policy, so their agreement provides a criterion for selecting transferable experience.

The distinction matters because a dynamics discrepancy and a discrepancy in learning value are different ways to assess the same source data. The authors identify limitations of dynamics-focused methods and develop their filter around cross-domain value consistency. Experiments with changes in kinematics and morphology show superior performance over prior approaches in the evaluated environments, supporting this selection strategy when target interaction is scarce.
neurips-2023-cross-domain-policy-adaptat.tldr: VGDF adapts policies across changed dynamics by sharing source experience whose value targets closely match those in the target domain.

paragraphs: Protein engineering often aims to change what a protein does while preserving its overall structural organization. Functionally important residues form active sites or binding surfaces, whereas other residues help establish the fold. Identifying which sequence patterns to modify is computationally difficult and typically requires substantial domain knowledge. This paper develops a data-driven way to separate those roles.

The proposed model combines a disentangled Wasserstein autoencoder with an auxiliary classifier. It isolates function-related patterns from the remaining representation, with theoretical guarantees for that separation. This organization enables protein sequences to be edited in one pass and makes the relationship between the editing action and the resulting sequence easier to understand.

The authors apply the method to T-cell receptors, where structure and function provide a suitable test case. They show that receptor function can be altered without changing the structural backbone. Against several competing methods, the approach improves generation quality and efficiency, using only 10% of the running time required by baseline models. These findings support targeted sequence editing through separated representations.
neurips-2023-disentangled-wasserstein-au.tldr: A disentangled autoencoder enables efficient T-cell receptor sequence edits that change function while preserving the structural backbone.

paragraphs: Effective robustness measures how much better a model handles shifted data than its in-distribution accuracy would predict. The comparison therefore depends on how in-distribution performance is measured. This paper argues that using one test set, such as ImageNet, becomes problematic when the models being compared were trained on substantially different data distributions.

The authors propose controlling for accuracy on multiple in-distribution test sets that collectively cover the evaluated models’ training distributions. This creates a broader reference for predicting out-of-distribution performance. The aim is to distinguish extra robustness from performance differences that become visible once the evaluation better represents each model’s training data.

Under this evaluation, the apparent effective-robustness advantages of zero-shot CLIP-like models diminish. The authors suggest that the revised reference may explain surprising gains reported when ImageNet was the only in-distribution test set. This is a qualified explanation about how robustness is measured: it shows that the estimated advantage depends on the comparison framework, rather than establishing that these models lack useful robustness.
neurips-2023-effective-robustness-agains.tldr: A robustness metric that accounts for multiple training distributions reduces the apparent extra robustness of zero-shot CLIP-like models.

paragraphs: A reusable skill in hierarchical reinforcement learning needs a goal, a policy for reaching it, and an initiation set describing where that policy can succeed. The last two must develop together. As the policy improves, earlier execution data can become outdated, making the learned initiation set inaccurate and harming the agent’s subsequent task performance.

The paper identifies three difficulties specific to this learning problem: changing data relevance, assigning credit over time, and pessimism. It addresses them with tools from off-policy value estimation and classification. The central aim is to keep the estimate of where a skill works aligned with the policy currently being learned.

Experiments show faster learning of higher-quality initiation sets in MiniGrid and Montezuma’s Revenge. The method also discovers promising robot grasps in Robosuite and improves a state-of-the-art option-discovery method on a difficult MuJoCo maze task. These results connect better initiation-set learning to practical decisions about when to invoke a skill, as well as to the quality of the skills an agent discovers.
neurips-2023-effectively-learning-initia.tldr: Combining off-policy value estimation with classification helps agents learn more accurately and quickly where their evolving skills will succeed.

paragraphs: This paper studies precision-matrix estimation for Gaussian distributions satisfying multivariate total positivity of order two, abbreviated MTP2. Under this assumption, the precision matrix has the structure of an M-matrix. Estimation can therefore be expressed as a log-determinant optimization problem with sign constraints, making the structural assumption part of the optimization itself.

Existing algorithms use block coordinate descent or proximal-point methods. Their computational burden grows in high dimensions because they must repeatedly solve nonnegative quadratic programs or large linear systems. The proposed alternative uses a two-metric projection method, combining a carefully chosen search direction with a scheme for partitioning variables.

These design choices substantially reduce computational complexity, and the authors establish theoretical convergence. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets also show significant efficiency improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The contribution is thus a faster way to solve this structured estimation problem, backed by both analysis and observed runtime behavior. Its scope is specifically precision estimation under the stated total-positivity assumption.
neurips-2023-fast-projected-newton-like-.tldr: A projected Newton-like algorithm makes precision-matrix estimation under MTP2 constraints more computationally efficient, with established convergence.

paragraphs: Bayesian inference depends on approximating a posterior distribution that may contain multiple plausible explanations and strong dependencies among variables. This paper uses neural samplers to represent such distributions implicitly through the samples they generate. The approach targets high-dimensional posteriors whose correlations and multiple modes are difficult to capture with simpler approximations.

The authors derive new inference bounds by locally linearizing the neural sampler. This provides a training approach distinct from methods requiring an additional discriminator and an unstable adversarial objective. They also introduce a sampler architecture using differentiable numerical approximations, enabling implicit distributions over tens of millions of latent variables.

Experiments show that the method can recover correlations across layers in large Bayesian neural networks, a capability the authors identify as important for performance and difficult to obtain at this scale. On downstream tasks, its expressive posterior approximations outperform state-of-the-art uncertainty-quantification methods. The results support both the computational feasibility of the architecture and the value of preserving richer dependencies in learned uncertainty.
neurips-2023-implicit-variational-infere.tldr: Neural samplers with new inference bounds scale rich implicit posterior approximations to tens of millions of variables.

paragraphs: The centers chosen at the start of a clustering algorithm can strongly affect its final quality. This paper develops an initialization method for k-median clustering in general metric spaces, including discrete spaces defined by graphs. Its aim is to provide good starting centers for subsequent local search, rather than treating initialization as a minor preliminary step.

The method constructs a tree representation through metric embedding and uses a new efficient search algorithm to select centers. Called HST initialization, it can produce lower-error initial centers than k-median++. The authors also report greater efficiency when the requested number of clusters is not too small, making that computational advantage explicitly conditional on k.

The initialization can be extended to differential privacy to generate private starting centers. Combined with differentially private local search, the private method improves previous approximation-error results and approaches a lower bound within a small factor. Experiments support the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The contribution connects better starting points with both ordinary clustering quality and the error guarantees available under privacy constraints.
neurips-2023-k-median-clustering-via-met.tldr: Tree-based HST initialization improves k-median starting centers and supports stronger approximation guarantees for differentially private clustering.

paragraphs: Regression can estimate outputs directly from examples using general relationships, or learn a function through an expensive training process. The first approach can struggle in high dimensions; the second can require substantial computation. This paper combines these approaches by learning a transductive system that can infer new functional relationships from a few input-output examples.

The theoretical foundation is vector-valued reproducing kernel Banach spaces. Using this framework, the authors show that transductive regression systems can be meta-learned with gradient descent. Their Transducer performs in-context approximation over both finite-dimensional spaces and infinite-dimensional spaces, extending the approach to operator regression, where the relationships involve functions.

Once trained, the Transducer can capture new relationships and produce image estimates almost immediately from a small example set. The authors demonstrate benefits for modeling physical systems affected by varying external factors, including partial differential equations and climate applications. In those demonstrations, the method uses little data and a fraction of usual deep-learning training costs, emphasizing the benefit of reusing a learned adaptation procedure.
neurips-2023-learning-functional-transdu.tldr: A meta-learned Transducer rapidly infers new functional relationships from a few examples, including in physical-system and climate-modeling applications.

paragraphs: Minigrid and Miniworld are libraries of goal-oriented environments for reinforcement-learning research, covering two-dimensional and three-dimensional settings. Their central design choice is minimalism: users should be able to build new environments quickly for specific research needs. The paper presents the libraries as research infrastructure whose usefulness comes partly from how easily researchers can customize them.

The authors explain the design philosophy, describe the environments, and present the interface for generating worlds. These components make environment construction an explicit part of the contribution. The abstract reports widespread adoption across the reinforcement-learning community, indicating that the libraries have supported work in a broad range of research areas.

A unified interface also connects the two libraries. The paper illustrates its capabilities through transfer-learning case studies involving both reinforcement-learning agents and humans moving between different observation spaces. These studies show how the shared interface supports questions that span environment representations. The contribution combines configurable environments with a common framework for examining transfer, with source code and documentation available for both libraries.
neurips-2023-minigrid-miniworld-modular-.tldr: Minigrid and Miniworld provide customizable 2D and 3D reinforcement-learning environments with a unified interface supporting transfer-learning studies.

paragraphs: An event in a video may be audible, visible, or both. Yet weak video-level labels often identify only which events occur, leaving their modality unspecified. This paper studies that unaligned setting on the Look, Listen, and Parse dataset, where assuming that sound and imagery always support the same prediction can mislead learning.

The proposed method, VALOR, uses large contrastively pretrained models as teachers to derive modality-specific event labels. These labels provide information missing from the original supervision. The authors find that independent audio and visual teachers outperform teachers that fuse modalities, attributing this advantage to avoiding noise from the other, potentially unaligned, source of information.

The harvested labels improve an attentional baseline by 8.0 points in average Type@AV F-score. The best model achieves state-of-the-art results across LLP metrics, including a 5.4-point Type@AV improvement. VALOR also extends to audio-visual event localization with state-of-the-art results. The findings support using modality-specific teachers when a video’s sound and imagery do not necessarily describe the same event.
neurips-2023-modality-independent-teache.tldr: VALOR uses separate audio and visual teachers to enrich weak event labels and improve parsing when the modalities are unaligned.

paragraphs: Randomized Q-learning, or RandQL, is a model-free algorithm for learning through repeated episodes while limiting regret. The authors present it as, to their knowledge, the first tractable model-free algorithm based on posterior sampling. Its defining mechanism is to randomize learning rates, creating optimistic exploration without adding explicit exploration bonuses.

The paper analyzes both tabular environments and settings with a metric state-action space. In the tabular case, the regret bound is approximately the square root of H⁵SAT, up to logarithmic factors. H is the planning horizon, S and A count states and actions, and T counts episodes. This expresses how the guarantee depends on both problem size and accumulated experience.

For metric spaces, the bound is approximately H^(5/2) T^((d_z+1)/(d_z+2)), again suppressing logarithmic factors, where d_z is the zooming dimension. Thus, the analysis extends beyond finite lookup-table representations and relates performance to the metric setting’s complexity. Experiments on baseline exploration environments show RandQL outperforming existing approaches, supporting learning-rate randomization as a practical exploration mechanism.
neurips-2023-model-free-posterior-sampli.tldr: RandQL randomizes learning rates to achieve bonus-free optimistic exploration, with regret guarantees in tabular and metric-space environments.

paragraphs: This paper examines why efficient mask-transformer models are difficult to train for panoptic segmentation. The authors identify an imbalance in the training objective: its complexity produces much stronger penalties for false positives. That imbalance makes end-to-end learning difficult, especially for the efficient models that are attractive when deployment computation is constrained.

ReMaX addresses the training process by introducing relaxation into both mask predictions and class predictions. These changes reduce the difficulty associated with the unbalanced objective. Because the relaxation is applied during training, the reported performance improvements do not require additional computation when the trained model is used for inference.

The authors report consistent improvements by clear margins. Combined with efficient backbones such as MobileNetV3-Small, ReMaX achieves state-of-the-art results for efficient panoptic segmentation on COCO, ADE20K, and Cityscapes. The findings emphasize that deployment efficiency depends partly on training design: improving how a compact architecture learns can improve its results while retaining its inference cost.
neurips-2023-remax-relaxing-for-better-t.tldr: ReMaX relaxes mask and class predictions during training to improve efficient panoptic segmentation without adding inference cost.

paragraphs: Dataset condensation seeks to create a small synthetic dataset useful for training models. Squeeze, Recover and Relabel, or SRe²L, changes how that synthetic data and the model are optimized. It decouples their bilevel optimization, aiming to make condensation practical across dataset sizes, network architectures, and image resolutions.

The framework supports synthesized images at arbitrary resolutions and reduces training cost and memory demands for high-resolution synthesis. It also supports scaling to arbitrary evaluation architectures. These properties address several connected obstacles: a condensation method must handle large source datasets, produce suitably detailed images, and remain useful across the networks trained on its output.

At 50 images per class, experiments report validation accuracies of 42.5% on Tiny-ImageNet and 60.8% on ImageNet-1K, exceeding previous state-of-the-art results by 14.5 and 32.9 percentage points. Against MTT during synthesis, reported speedups are about 52-fold for ConvNet-4 and 16-fold for ResNet-18, with 11.6-fold and 6.4-fold lower memory consumption. These results demonstrate both predictive utility and substantial computational savings in the evaluated configurations.
neurips-2023-squeeze-recover-and-relabel.tldr: SRe²L decouples model and synthetic-data optimization to scale dataset condensation while improving accuracy, synthesis speed, and memory use.

paragraphs: Finite-element simulations use meshes whose resolution affects both accuracy and computational cost. Adaptive mesh refinement concentrates detail where it is useful, but traditional approaches rely on task-specific rules or expensive error estimates. This paper develops a learned refinement method intended to handle challenging simulations beyond the simple examples supported by earlier learned approaches.

The method treats mesh elements as collaborating agents that can split into new agents as refinement proceeds. This adaptive swarm formulation supports spatial rewards, making it easier to identify which local decisions deserve credit. Message-passing networks let neighboring elements exchange information, connecting local refinement choices to the surrounding mesh.

Experiments show reliable, scalable, and efficient strategies across the tested problems. The method achieves up to a thirtyfold computational speedup compared with uniform refinement in complex simulations. It also outperforms learned baselines and matches the refinement quality of a traditional error-based strategy without expensive oracle error information. These results support learning where to spend simulation computation through coordinated local decisions.
neurips-2023-swarm-reinforcement-learnin.tldr: ASMR learns coordinated local mesh refinement, achieving up to thirtyfold speedups over uniform refinement in the evaluated complex simulations.

paragraphs: Graph attention faces a tension between local detail and distant information. Local attention inherits difficulties from message passing when information must travel far. Global attention can reach across the graph but fail to represent the hierarchy of neighborhoods and their finer structure. This paper introduces Subtree Attention, or STA, to address both concerns.

STA organizes attention around rooted subtrees and directly computes attention weights among neighbors several hops away. This makes distance through the graph part of the attention design. The authors prove that STA approximates global attention under extreme settings, connecting the proposed neighborhood-aware construction to a fully attentional formulation.

An efficient version uses kernelized softmax to obtain linear time complexity. The resulting STAGNN architecture combines STA with a hop-aware attention strategy. Across ten node-classification datasets, STA-based models outperform existing graph transformers and mainstream graph neural networks. The findings support attention that can access multi-hop information while retaining the neighborhood organization that global attention may overlook.
neurips-2023-tailoring-self-attention-fo.tldr: Subtree Attention combines direct multi-hop attention with graph neighborhood structure, improving node classification through an efficient linear-time formulation.

paragraphs: Local Bayesian optimization has shown strong empirical performance on high-dimensional problems compared with traditional global strategies. A common explanation is that focusing locally avoids the curse of dimensionality. This paper examines that intuition more carefully by studying both the quality of local solutions and the convergence behavior of a particular local optimization algorithm.

First, the authors analyze individual local solutions of functions drawn from a Gaussian process. They find that these solutions have surprisingly favorable statistics compared with what one would expect global methods to recover. This provides evidence relevant to why a local search strategy can work well, even when it does not pursue a global search directly.

The paper then gives the first rigorous analysis of a previously proposed Bayesian local optimization algorithm and derives convergence rates with both noisy and noiseless observations. These are guarantees for the analyzed procedure and settings. Together, the results replace part of the informal explanation for local optimization’s success with concrete statements about solution behavior and convergence.
neurips-2023-the-behavior-and-convergenc.tldr: The paper studies why local Bayesian optimization performs well and establishes convergence rates for a specific algorithm with and without observation noise.

paragraphs: Covariate shift arises when source and target data have different input distributions. Methods for handling it are often studied separately for particular learning tasks, leaving a fragmented theoretical picture. This paper develops a unified analysis of nonparametric learning in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, aiming to cover a broad range of prediction objectives.

The analysis applies to a rich family of loss functions. It includes mean regression, quantile regression, likelihood-based classification, and margin-based classification as special cases. This breadth matters because it brings several distinct ways of defining prediction error into one framework for understanding learning under changed input distributions.

The authors study two types of covariate-shift problems and establish sharp convergence rates for the general loss setting. Their results agree with known optimal results when the loss is squared error, connecting the broader framework to an established case. Numerical studies on synthetic and real examples support the theory and demonstrate the proposed method’s effectiveness across the evaluated problems.
neurips-2023-towards-a-unified-analysis-.tldr: A unified kernel-learning analysis establishes sharp convergence rates under covariate shift for a broad family of regression and classification losses.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a network to acquire new tasks while retaining earlier knowledge. A central obstacle is catastrophic forgetting, where learning something new damages previous capabilities. Existing approaches often emphasize separate strategies such as regularizing weights, replaying experience, or isolating parameters. This paper argues for combining mechanisms so their strengths can work together.

Inspired by the brain’s concurrent use of multiple learning processes, TriRE organizes learning around retention, revision, and preparation for future tasks. It retains the most prominent neurons for each task, revises and strengthens knowledge from current and past tasks, and promotes less active neurons through rewinding and relearning.

These components address both preserving useful knowledge and making network capacity available for subsequent learning. Across the continual-learning settings studied, TriRE significantly reduces interference between tasks and outperforms approaches considered in isolation. The findings support coordinating several learning mechanisms within one paradigm, with the reported benefit expressed as improved retention and reduced conflict during sequential learning.
neurips-2023-trire-a-multi-mechanism-lea.tldr: TriRE combines neuron retention, knowledge revision, and rewinding with relearning to reduce interference and forgetting across sequential tasks.

paragraphs: Off-policy learning improves a policy using feedback logged by an earlier decision-making system. The probabilities with which that system selected actions are often unknown and must be estimated. Treating those estimates as exact can introduce both bias and variance, especially for examples assigned small, inaccurate logging probabilities.

This paper makes uncertainty in the estimated logging policy an explicit part of learning. Its Uncertainty-aware Inverse Propensity Score estimator, UIPS, adjusts instance reweighting to account for that uncertainty. The goal is to prevent unreliable estimates from having the damaging influence they can acquire when used directly in off-policy optimization.

The authors provide a theoretical convergence guarantee and evaluate the method on synthetic data and real-world recommendation datasets. UIPS significantly improves the quality of the learned policy compared with an extensive set of state-of-the-art baselines. The findings identify logging-policy uncertainty as a consequential part of the learning problem: accounting for uncertainty in the data-collection process can improve the decisions learned from its records.
neurips-2023-uncertainty-aware-instance-.tldr: UIPS accounts for uncertainty in estimated logging probabilities to improve off-policy learning from recorded feedback.

paragraphs: Weakly open-vocabulary semantic segmentation learns to identify image regions for arbitrary classes using image-text pairs. Existing methods use group tokens to cluster image features and align those groups with text. This paper identifies a mismatch: groups receive all-to-one alignment during training but are used through one-to-one alignment at inference, leaving individual groups insufficiently supervised.

The authors address this gap with non-learnable prototypical regularization, or NPR. Prototypes estimated from source features provide supervision for contrastive matching of group tokens. The intended effect is to make groups less redundant while capturing more complete semantic regions, improving both the compactness and richness of their representations.

The resulting PGSeg network draws prototypical information from images and text at multiple levels. These varied sources progressively strengthen segmentation through multimodal regularization. Experiments achieve state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks. The contribution therefore links a specific training-versus-inference mismatch to a supervision mechanism that gives individual group tokens clearer semantic roles, while retaining the image-text training setting.
neurips-2023-uncovering-prototypical-kno.tldr: PGSeg uses image and text prototypes to supervise individual group tokens, improving weakly supervised open-vocabulary segmentation.
